Rashi on Niddah 44a:12:1.hebrew: כנעוריה - ושבה אל בית אביה כנעוריה, כלומר: אם דומה לימי נעורים, ושבה, ואם לאו, לא תשוב:
Rashi on Niddah 44a:12:1.english: As in her youth - [The verse states:] "And she shall return to her father's house as in her youth" — that is to say: If she is similar to the days of [her] youth, she shall return; and if not, she shall not return.

Rashi on Niddah 44a:15:1.english: The verses are resolved - In that both of them are necessary.

Rashi on Niddah 44a:15:2.hebrew: אלא מתניתין - מדנקט יום אחד ולא נקט עובר, דוקא נקט:
Rashi on Niddah 44a:15:2.english: Rather, the mishna - Since [the mishna] stated "one day" and did not state "a fetus," it stated [this] precisely.

Rashi on Niddah 44a:15:3.hebrew: אמר רב ששת - האי פוסל לאו אאמו קאי, אלא אעבדיו קאי, והכא בכהן שהיו לו שתי נשים וכו':
Rashi on Niddah 44a:15:3.english: Rav Sheshet said - This "disqualifies" does not refer to his mother, but rather refers to his [father's] slaves; and here [we are dealing] with a priest who had two wives, etc.

Rashi on Niddah 44a:15:4.english: One who is a divorcée - That she was a divorcée, and he transgressed and married her.

Rashi on Niddah 44a:15:5.hebrew: ויש לו בנים משאינה גרושה - והן כהנים כשרים, ועבדים שנפלו להן בירושה אוכלין בתרומה בשבילן, דכתיב (ויקרא כ״ב:י״א) וכהן כי יקנה נפש קנין כספו וגו':
Rashi on Niddah 44a:15:5.english: And he has sons from the wife who is not a divorcée - And they are valid priests, and slaves who fell to them through inheritance may eat terumah on their account, as it is written (Leviticus 22:11): "And if a priest acquires a person, the acquisition of his money, etc."

Rashi on Niddah 44a:15:6.hebrew: ויש לו בן יום אחד מן הגרושה - והוא חלל ואינו ראוי לכהונה, ויש לו חלק בעבדים, ופוסל את כולן מן התרומה, שאין אנו יודעין לברור מי מגיע לחלקו. ודוקא בן יום אחד, דראוי לירושה, אבל כל זמן שלא נולד, אוכלין כולן, דאין זכייה לעובר:
Rashi on Niddah 44a:15:6.english: And he has a one-day-old son from the divorcée - And he is a chalal [a disqualified priest] and is not fit for the priesthood, and he has a share in the slaves, and disqualifies all of them from [eating] terumah, as we do not know how to determine which [slave] falls to his share. And specifically a one-day-old [child], who is eligible to inherit; but as long as he has not been born, all of them may eat [terumah], for there is no acquisition for a fetus.

Rashi on Niddah 44a:16:1.hebrew: ולאפוקי מדר' יוסי - דאמר במסכת יבמות בפרק אלמנה לכהן גדול (יבמות דף סז.) יש לו זכייה, ואפילו הוא במעי אשה זרה הכשרה לכהונה פוסלה, דקסבר: כל זמן שהוא במעי זרה זר הוא, וכל שכן האי דבמעי גרושה הוא, דאפילו כשיולד לא יהא ראוי:
Rashi on Niddah 44a:16:1.english: And to exclude [the opinion] of Rabbi Yosei - Who said in tractate Yevamot, in the chapter [entitled] 'A Widow to a High Priest' (Yevamot 67a), that [a fetus] has the right of acquisition, and even when he is in the womb of a non-priestly woman who is fit for the priesthood, he disqualifies her, for he holds: As long as he is in the womb of a non-priestess, he is a non-priest; and all the more so this [one], who is in the womb of a divorcée, for even when he is born he will not be fit [for the priesthood].

Rashi on Niddah 44a:17:1.english: To his paternal brother - For there is no inheritance except to the relatives of the father.

Rashi on Niddah 44a:17:2.hebrew: אי בעי מאבוה לירת - אפי' חשיבנא ליה כמאן דליתיה, ירתי לאחר מיתת אביהם, ואיהו מאי אהני:
Rashi on Niddah 44a:17:2.english: If he wishes, let him inherit from his father - Even if we consider him as though he does not exist, they inherit after the death of their father, and what did he accomplish?

Rashi on Niddah 44a:18:1.hebrew: נוחל בנכסי האם - אם מתה אמו ביום שנולד, הרי הוא יורשה. וכשמת הוא, באין אחיו מאביו ויורשין הימנו נכסי אמו, דאי לאו איהו, הוו שקלי ליה קרובי האם, דבן נוחל את אמו. אבל האם אינה נוחלת את בנה, וכל שכן קרובי האם שאין נוחלין אותו, דכתיב (במדבר א׳:ב׳): ״למשפחותם לבית אבותם״ — משפחת האם אינה קרויה משפחה:
Rashi on Niddah 44a:18:1.english: Inherits the mother's property - If his mother died on the day he was born, he inherits from her. And when he dies, his brothers from his father come and inherit his mother's property from him, for if not for him, the mother's relatives would have taken it, as a son inherits from his mother. But a mother does not inherit from her son, and all the more so the mother's relatives do not inherit from him, as it is written (Numbers 1:2): "By their families, according to their fathers' houses" — the mother's family is not called a family.

Rashi on Niddah 44a:18:2.hebrew: אבל עובר - שבמעיה, אם מתה מעוברת, אינו נוחל להנחיל את קרוביו מן האב:
Rashi on Niddah 44a:18:2.english: But a fetus - Which is in her womb; if she died while pregnant, it does not inherit [from her] to bequeath to its paternal relatives.

Rashi on Niddah 44a:1:1.english: And inherits and bequeaths - It is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Niddah 44a:1:2.english: Like a full-fledged groom - It is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Niddah 44a:2:1.hebrew: אשה - ואשה כי תהיה זבה וגו', והאי קרא בנדה משתעי:
Rashi on Niddah 44a:2:1.english: A woman - [The verse states:] "And if a woman has an issue, etc.," and this verse is speaking of a menstruating woman.

Rashi on Niddah 44a:3:1.english: [A girl] ten days old, etc. - [The Tanna] is expounding [the verse]: "And if a woman has an issue of her blood."

Rashi on Niddah 44a:6:1.hebrew: אדם - משמע כל שהוא מין אדם, אפילו קטן, כדכתיב (במדבר ל״א:ל״ה) ונפש אדם מן הנשים וגו', ובקטנות משתעי קרא:
Rashi on Niddah 44a:6:1.english: A person - [This] implies anyone who is of the human species, even a minor, as it is written (Numbers 31:35): "And human persons from among the women," etc., and the verse is speaking of female minors.

Rashi on Niddah 44a:7:1.english: Souls - Anyone in whom there is a soul.

Tosafot on Niddah 44a:12:1.hebrew: כנעוריה פרט למעוברת - ואם תאמר, תיפוק ליה מוזרע אין לה, עיין עליה, כי היכי דפסלינן בריש החולץ (יבמות לה:) חליצת מעוברת מאין לו, עיין עליו. וי"ל, דהתם לא קאמר אלא עיין והמתן אם יהיה ולד של קיימא, אבל לא מיפטרא מן היבום משום דכתיב אין לו; וה"נ לא מיפסלא מן התרומה בהכי:
Tosafot on Niddah 44a:12:1.english: "As in her youth" excludes a pregnant woman - And if you say: Let it be derived from "and has no child" (ve-zera ein lah) — [read as] "inspect her" (ayein aleha), just as we invalidate in the beginning of [Perek] HaCholetz (Yevamot 35b) the chalitzah of a pregnant woman based on "he has no [child]" (ein lo) — [read as] "inspect him" (ayein alav)? And one can say that there, it means only: inspect and wait [to see] if it will be a viable offspring; but she is not exempted from levirate marriage (yibbum) [merely] because it is written "he has no [child]." And so too here, she would not be disqualified from [eating] terumah by this [alone].

Tosafot on Niddah 44a:15:1.hebrew: אמר רב ששת הכא במאי עסקינן בכהן שיש לו ב' נשים - וא"ת: למה לי ב' נשים? לוקמה באשה אחת גרושה ויש לו בן אחד ממנה, דדוקא בן יום אחד פוסל ולא עובר, ואכלי העבדים בשביל כל המשפחה כולה לרבנן דר' יוסי, כדאמר ביבמות בפרק אלמנה (דף סז.). ועוד הקשה ה"ר אפרים, דבפרק מי שמת (ב"ב דף קמב.) אמר רב ששת: אחד זה ואחד זה קנה, בין מזכה לעובר בין לכשתלד; ופריך ליה ממתני' דבן יום אחד נוחל אבל עובר לא, ומשני דהתם משום דאיהו מיית ברישא. והשתא, ליפרוך מרישא: דבן יום אחד פוסל אבל עובר לא, משום דעובר לית ליה זכייה, כדמפרש הכא רב ששת גופיה, ולא ה"מ לשנויי מידי! וי"ל, דסבר רב ששת דלרבנן דר' יוסי נמי עובר אית ליה זכייה; וטעמא דעובר אינו פוסל משום: סמוך מיעוטא דמפילות למחצה דנקבות, והוה ליה זכרים מיעוטא, ולמיעוטא לא חיישינן כדחייש רבי יוסי. ולהכי אוקי הכא בכהן שיש לו ב' נשים ויש לו בנים משאינה גרושה, דכיון דיש לו בנים, לא פסיל עובר, אף ע"ג דיש לו זכייה, דלא חיישינן למיעוט הזכרים כדפי'; אבל אם אין לו בנים, פוסל עובר גם לרבנן, דאית ליה זכייה, דבין הוא זכר בין היא נקבה הרי הן שלה. ופליג רב ששת אשמואל, דאמר בפרק אלמנה (יבמות דף סז.) דלרבנן אוכלין בשביל כל המשפחה כולה, דסבר שמואל דלרבנן לית ליה זכייה לעובר. והשתא ניחא הא דקאמר התם רב ששת: מנא אמינא לה? דתניא: גר שמת כו', ולא דחי ליה דהך ברייתא כר' יוסי, דרבנן נמי לא פליגי אלא דלא חיישי למיעוטא, כדפי'. ואם תאמר, דבפרק מי שמת (ב"ב דף קמב.), גבי גר שמת ובזבזו ישראל נכסיו והיתה אשתו מעוברת לא קנו, שמעו אחרי כן שהפילה אשתו המחזיק בשניה קנה, בראשונה לא קנה — אמאי לא קנה המחזיק בראשונה, כיון דלבסוף הפילה? הא בפ' אלמנה (יבמות סז:) אמרינן דזכרים הוו מיעוטא משום מיעוטא דמפילות, ואין לעובר שסופו להיות נפל חלק בעבדים! וי"ל, דהתם משום דתלינן שמא כבר בשעת אכילת העבדים מת העובר בבטן, ולית ליה זכייה:
Tosafot on Niddah 44a:15:1.english: Rav Sheshet said: Here we are dealing with a priest who has two wives - And if you should say: Why do I need two wives? Let him establish [the mishna] with one wife [who is] a divorcée and he has one son from her, so that specifically a one-day-old [child] disqualifies and not a fetus, and the slaves would eat [teruma] on account of the entire family according to the Rabbis [who dispute] Rabbi Yosei, as [Shmuel] says in Yevamot in perek Almanah (67a)? And furthermore, Rabbeinu Ephraim raised a difficulty: For in perek Mi Shemet (Bava Batra 142a), Rav Sheshet said: In both this case and that case he acquires — whether one transfers ownership to a fetus, or [says it should take effect] when she gives birth. And [the Gemara there] challenged him from our mishna: "A one-day-old [baby] inherits," but a fetus does not. And [the Gemara] answered that there, it is because he dies first [before his mother]. But now, let it challenge [him] from the first clause [of our mishna]: that a one-day-old [child] disqualifies, but a fetus does not, because a fetus has no [capacity for] acquisition, as Rav Sheshet himself explains here, and it would not have been able to offer any answer! And one can say that Rav Sheshet maintains that according to the Rabbis [who dispute] Rabbi Yosei as well, a fetus has [the capacity for] acquisition. And the reason a fetus does not disqualify [the slaves] is because: attach the minority of miscarriages to the half of females, and males become a minority, and we do not take a minority into concern as Rabbi Yosei does. And for this reason, he established [the case] here as a priest who has two wives and has sons from the one who is not a divorcée, for since he has sons, the fetus does not disqualify [the slaves] even though it has [the capacity for] acquisition, because we do not take the minority of males into concern, as explained. But if he does not have sons, the fetus would disqualify [the slaves] according to the Rabbis as well, as it has [the capacity for] acquisition, for whether it is a male or a female, they [the slaves] belong to it. And Rav Sheshet disagrees with Shmuel, who said in perek Almanah (Yevamot 67a) that according to the Rabbis, [the slaves] eat on account of the entire family; for Shmuel maintains that according to the Rabbis, a fetus has no [capacity for] acquisition. And now, what Rav Sheshet said there is well-understood: "From where do I say [that a fetus acquires]? As it is taught: A convert who died, etc.," and [the Gemara] did not reject [his proof by arguing] that this baraita is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, because the Rabbis also do not disagree [that a fetus acquires], but rather they merely do not take a minority into concern, as explained. And if you should say: In perek Mi Shemet (Bava Batra 142a), regarding a convert who died and Israelites plundered his property, and his wife was pregnant — they did not acquire; [if] they subsequently heard that his wife miscarried — one who took possession the second time acquired, [but] in the first time he did not acquire. Why did the one who took possession the first time not acquire, given that in the end she miscarried? For in perek Almanah (Yevamot 67b) we say that males are a minority on account of the minority of miscarriages, and a fetus that is destined to be a non-viable birth (nefel) has no share in the slaves! And one can say that there [in Yevamot, regarding the slaves], it is because we attribute [it to the possibility that] perhaps already at the time the slaves were eating, the fetus had died in the womb and has no [capacity for] acquisition:

Tosafot on Niddah 44a:17:1.hebrew: ואי בעי מיניה לירות כו' - וא"ת, דבפרק מי שמת (ב"ב קמב.) דפריך לרב ששת מהך דבן יום א' נוחל ומנחיל, אבל עובר לא, ומשני: נוחל את האם להנחיל לאחים מן האב; והשתא, מה היתה סברת המקשה? דע"כ צריך לומר כדמשני רב ששת, דאי לאו הכי תקשה ליה: אי בעי מיניה לירות, אי בעי מאבוה לירות, כדמקשה הכא. וי"ל, דיפרש כמר בריה דרב יוסף שממעט בחלק בכורה, אבל עובר לא, ולאו משום וילדו לו, אלא משום דעובר לית ליה זכייה. א"נ, ידע שפיר כדמשני רב ששת: נוחל את האם להנחיל לאחיו מן האב, אך היה סבור דאיהי מייתא ברישא, וקאמר: עובר לא, משום דלא קנה. ובשילהי פ"ק דערכין (דף ז.), דאמר שמואל: אשה שיצתה ליהרג מכין אותה כנגד הריון שלה כדי שימות הולד תחלה, הא לאו הכי הולד מת לבסוף, ופריך ליה מהא דבן יום אחד נוחל, אלמא ולד מת תחלה; הוה מצי לשנויי: אבל עובר לא, לומר שממעט בחלק בכור כדאמר בשמעתין, אלא דניחא ליה לאוקמי מילתא דרב ששת, דאמר הכא איהו מיית ברישא, אליבא דשמואל, ולחלק האמת, שיש חילוק בין מתה לנהרגה:
Tosafot on Niddah 44a:17:1.english: And if he wants, let him inherit from him, etc. - And should you say: In the chapter [entitled] "Mi Shemet" (Bava Batra 142a), where [the Gemara] objects to Rav Sheshet from this [mishna], that a one-day-old [child] inherits and bequeaths, but a fetus does not, and [Rav Sheshet] resolves [it]: [he] inherits [the property of] the mother to bequeath to [his] brothers from the father; and now, what was the reasoning of the objector? For perforce one must say as Rav Sheshet answered, because if it were not so, it should be difficult for him: "If he wants, let him inherit from him; if he wants, let him inherit from his father," just as [the Gemara] objects here! And it can be answered: He [the objector] could explain [the mishna] in accordance with Mar bar Rav Yosef, that [the one-day-old child] reduces the portion of the firstborn, but a fetus does not; and [this is] not because of [the verse] "and they bear him [children]" (Deuteronomy 21:15), but rather because a fetus has no [capacity for] acquisition. Alternatively, he [the objector] well knew [that the mishna is explained] as Rav Sheshet answered, [namely, that he] inherits [the property of] the mother to bequeath to his brothers from the father; however, he believed that she died first, and [the mishna] states "a fetus does not [inherit]" because he did not acquire. And at the end of the first chapter of Arakhin (7a), where Shmuel said: [With regard to] a woman who went out to be executed, they strike her against her womb so that the fetus will die first, [which implies that] otherwise, the fetus dies last; and [the Gemara] objects to him from this [mishna], that a one-day-old [child] inherits [and bequeaths, but a fetus does not], which shows that the fetus dies first — [the Gemara] could have answered: "but a fetus does not" [comes] to say that [a fetus] does not reduce the portion of the firstborn, as is said in our sugya; rather, it preferred to establish the statement of Rav Sheshet, who said here "he dies first," in accordance with Shmuel, and to state the true distinction, that there is a difference between [a woman who] died [naturally] and [one who] was executed.

Tosafot on Niddah 44a:18:1.hebrew: איהו מיית ברישא - והא דתנן בפ' בהמה המקשה (חולין דף עד.) השוחט את הבהמה ומצא בה בן ט' חי, יש חילוק בין מתה לנהרגה, כדאמר בערכין (דף ז.). והא דאמר נמי בהשוחט במתה אמה והדר ילידתיה, היינו נמי כשנהרגה; אי נמי, כגון דמתה אמו מחמת לידה, דכיון דעקר הולד לצאת אז לא מיית, כדאמר שמואל שילהי פ"ק דערכין (דף ז.): ישבה על המשבר ומתה, מחתכין אותה בשבת ומוציאין הולד. וא"ת: אם כן, עובר נוחל ומנחיל בישבה על המשבר ומתה תחלה? י"ל: דאין הכי נמי, ונקט בן יום אחד משום דפסיקא ליה דנוחל ומנחיל, אבל עובר לא פסיקא ליה. ומיהא, בן יום אחד ההורגו חייב דקתני, אבל עובר לא — היינו אפילו נהרגה או ישבה על המשבר, עד שיצא ראשו, כדתנן במסכת אהלות פ"ז (משנה ו) ומייתי לה בפרק בן סורר ומורה (סנהדרין דף עב:): אשה המקשה, חותך אבר; יצא ראשו, אין דוחין נפש מפני נפש. ומיהו, אפשר דדוקא היכא דאמו חיה לא מיחייב ההורגו עד שיצא ראשו, שתלוי קצת בחיות אמו; אבל היכא דמתה חייב, משום דכמונח בקופסא דמי. וא"ת: אם תמצי לומר דמותר להורגו בבטן אפי' מתה אמו ולא הוי כמונח בקופסא, אמאי מחללין עליו את השבת שמביאין סכין דרך ר"ה לקרוע האם, כדמוכח בפ' קמא דערכין (דף ז:)? וי"ל: דמכל מקום משום פקוח נפש מחללין עליו את השבת, אף ע"ג דמותר להרגו; דהא גוסס בידי אדם, ההורגו פטור, כדאמר פרק הנשרפין (סנהדרין עח.) דרוב גוססים למיתה, ומחללין את השבת עליו, כדאמר פרק בתרא דיומא (ד' פד:) דאין מהלכין בפקוח נפש אחר הרוב:
Tosafot on Niddah 44a:18:1.english: He dies first - And [as for] that which we learned in the chapter [entitled] "Behema HaMaksheh" (Chullin 74a), "One who slaughters an animal and finds within it a live nine-[month-old fetus]" — there is a distinction between [where the mother] died [naturally] and [where she] was killed, as [the Gemara] says in Arakhin (7a). And that which [the Gemara] also says in [the chapter entitled] "HaShoḥet" [Chullin 38a], regarding [a case where] its mother died and afterward gave birth to it — that is also [referring to a case] where she was killed; alternatively, [it refers to a case] where its mother died as a result of childbirth, for once the fetus has dislodged [itself] to emerge, it does not die [first] at that point, as Shmuel said at the end of the first chapter of Arakhin (7a): "[If a woman] sat upon the birthstool (mashber) and died, they cut into her on Shabbat and extract the fetus." And if you say: If so, a fetus should inherit and bequeath [in a case where the mother] sat upon the birthstool and died first? One can say [in response]: Indeed, so it is [that it inherits and bequeaths in that case]; and [the Mishna] specified a one-day-old [child] because it is definitive [for it] that it inherits and bequeaths, whereas [for] a fetus it is not definitive [as it usually dies before the mother]. However, that which [the Mishna] teaches, [that regarding] a one-day-old [child] one who kills him is liable [for murder], but [for] a fetus [he is] not — that applies even if [the mother] was killed or sat upon the birthstool, until its head has emerged. As we learned in tractate Oholot, chapter 7 (Mishnah 6), and it is cited in the chapter [entitled] "Ben Sorer UMoreh" (Sanhedrin 72b): "[If] a woman is having difficult labor, one cuts [the fetus] limb [by limb; but once] its head has emerged, one does not set aside one life for another life." And yet, it is possible that specifically where its mother is alive, one who kills it is not liable until its head has emerged, since [its life] is somewhat dependent upon the life of its mother; but where [the mother] died, he is liable, because it is considered like [an object] placed in a box. And if you say: If you conclude that it is permitted to kill it in the womb even if its mother died, and it is not considered like [something] placed in a box, [then] why do we desecrate Shabbat for its sake, in that they bring a knife through the public domain to cut open the mother, as is proven in the first chapter of Arakhin (7b)? And one can say [in response]: Nevertheless, on account of saving a life (pikku'aḥ nefesh), we desecrate Shabbat for its sake, even though it would be permitted to kill it. For behold, [in the case of] one who is moribund at the hands of man (goses bi-yedei adam), one who kills him is exempt, as [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] "HaNisrafin" (Sanhedrin 78a), because the majority of moribund people are headed for death; yet we desecrate Shabbat for his sake, as [the Gemara] says in the final chapter of Yoma (84b), because we do not follow the majority with regard to saving a life.
